rationale: ExpenseOwl is a real, public, permissively licensed (MIT — LICENSE verified verbatim: "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2024 Tanishq Rupaal") Go+vanilla-JS self-hosted expense tracker (~1.5k stars, 154 commits on main) whose defining core matches the leaf exactly: (1) the expense record as a money-out event with name/purpose, category, amount and date (internal/storage/storage.go: `type Expense struct { ID, RecurringID, Name, Tags, Category, Amount, Currency, Date }`), (2) user-manageable spending categories as the backbone of analysis (`Config{Categories, Currency, StartDate}`, `defaultCategories` preset set, `ValidateCategory()` sanitizing/validating category names, plus a user-driven Category Settings page that adds, removes, drag-reorders and saves categories via PUT /categories/edit), and (3) a live aggregated view over the records — internal/web/templates/index.html computes `calculateCategoryBreakdown()` (per-category totals and percentages) and a month Total from `getMonthExpenses(allExpenses)`, rendered as a doughnut chart plus a per-category legend with totals, while internal/web/templates/functions.js supplies `getMonthBounds()` (calendar month when startDay=1) and `formatCurrency()` with a `cny` entry (¥, two decimals, Intl.NumberFormat). The leaf's key boundary is respected: the README states "The primary intention is to track spending across your categories in a simplistic manner… This is *not* a budgeting app; it's for tracking", so the organizing object is the record plus its categories, not a plan container — exactly the Expense Tracking Application, not a Budgeting/PFM app. The scenario's review loop maps1:1 onto the source: internal/web/templates/table.html provides a month-scoped detail table (prev/next month buttons switch adjacent months), inline edit of name/category/amount/date and delete; internal/api/handlers.go exposes AddExpense/EditExpense/DeleteExpense/GetExpenses plus GetCategories/UpdateCategories, and every save re-reads all records and recomputes the month total and category breakdown immediately, so corrections propagate into the aggregates on the fly. Persistence across restarts is real and local: internal/storage/jsonStore.go writes data/expenses.json and data/config.json under a mutex (single-user, no auth, no bank sync), matching the "本机单用户…重开保留" constraint. Deliberate deltas the template author must implement rather than copy: upstream stores `Amount float64` with expenses as negative values, whereas the scenario requires positive amounts held as integer cents (int64) with strict two-decimal rendering and no floating-point accumulation; upstream allows a configurable month start day (default 1) while the scenario fixes natural calendar months; upstream's category list is a flat string array with no inline rename and no cascade into existing records, so a rename control plus category-id/rename propagation must be added; and upstream's P0-excluded extras (income/gain, recurring transactions, cashflow panel, tags, CSV import/export, PWA service worker) are trimmed for the P0 scope. Selected files total well under 180KB each (largest ~30KB) and cover licence, docs, domain model, local persistence, HTTP surface, and the three user-facing surfaces (dashboard summary, month-scoped detail table, category management).

alternatives.status: verified real (the supplied lead) but rejected
alternatives.why: LICENSE fetched verbatim is GNU General Public License v2.0 — copyleft, not permissive, and the C++/Qt/CMake desktop codebase is enormous, so a small pinned source surface is impractical. It also models money as double and spans accounts/budgets/stocks, pulling the shape toward Personal Finance Management rather than a minimal local record tracker.

LICENSE fetched verbatim is GNU AGPL-3.0 (network copyleft, incompatible with permissive reuse expectations), and the PHP/Laravel + Vue codebase is very large; it also brings multi-currency, accounts and budget envelopes that exceed the scenario's P0 scope.

Technically the strongest money-model match — it stores amounts as integer cents, which is exactly what the scenario's "整数分存储、不使用浮点累计" asks for. Rejected on application type: it is a plan-first budgeting app (envelopes, rules, accounts, sync), which the leaf explicitly flags as the sibling to stay away from, so its centre of gravity is the wrong one for an expense-tracking leaf.

search_notes: Read the authoritative input.json and then the full leaf.md (217 lines, read in one pass; no content_file was present in the leaf object). The workspace itself only exposed input.json and leaf.md — manifest.json, inventory.json, allowed-files.json and README.md were all unreadable (permission denied), and api.github.com was blocked for webfetch, so verification was done through raw.githubusercontent.com file fetches and github.com HTML tree views, which is how every listed path was confirmed to exist with the described content. Search path: websearch for "open source personal expense tracker minimal categories monthly summary integer cents sqlite" and "github expense tracker self-hosted simple flask sqlite categories monthly total MIT license", which surfaced the GitHub topic pages for expense-tracker / personal-expense-tracker / personal-finance-tracker and candidates including Tanq16/ExpenseOwl, Anoopnk/FinXpert, rogi2709/spendlocal, kapaj-ina/expense-tracker and several Flask/Next.js demo trackers. ExpenseOwl was selected after reading its README and source rather than its marketing text, because it is MIT, single-user, record-first, and actually ships category management plus month-scoped aggregation code (calculateCategoryBreakdown, getMonthExpenses, getMonthBounds, UpdateCategories). Its README, LICENSE, internal/storage/storage.go, internal/storage/jsonStore.go, internal/api/handlers.go, cmd/expenseowl/main.go and internal/web/templates/{functions.js,index.html,table.html,settings.html} were each fetched directly and confirmed; internal/web/templates/chart.min.js was deliberately excluded because the vendored minified Chart.js bundle is near/over the 180KB per-file ceiling and adds no design value. The lead was independently verified: moneymanagerex/moneymanagerex is real and its LICENSE is GPL-2.0, so it is listed only as an alternative, not selected. No commit hash, tag, branch URL or extra license claim is asserted anywhere in this result — only the repository URL, the eight verified file paths, and the license text actually read from the repository's own LICENSE file.
